original_test_intent: Physically inspect and cycle the specified Mellanox BF3 board, verify the correct slot, edge connector, retention, attached cables and clearance, then confirm after the approved reboot that the same board, ports and links are detected without new errors.
original_method: A trained operator binds the BF3 board part/serial and PCIe identity to its chassis slot, captures physical and Mellanox pre-state, drains affected workloads and links, establishes ESD and power isolation, removes and reseats the board once per approved service procedure, restores retention/cables/chassis, then compares PCIe, firmware, port/link, driver and error evidence after reboot.
manual_activity: A trained operator identifies, inspects and reseats the exact BF3 board, restores retention and dependent cables, and observes reboot/recovery; the owner reviews physical, PCIe and network evidence.
required_inputs: SUT/chassis, BF3 board part/serial/firmware/PCIe identity and exact slot/connector/retention/cable map
Approved board service procedure, workload/traffic drain, cycle count, power-state and ESD requirements
Expected PCIe device, Mellanox port/link/firmware/driver/error state and recovery window
Independent console/network recovery plus spare board/slot escalation plan
Camera/evidence labeling, operator identity and no-log-clear policy
safety_requirements: Only a trained operator may handle the BF3 board under approved traffic-drain, ESD and power-safe controls
Do not remove or insert the board energized unless the service procedure explicitly authorizes this exact platform operation
Stop on wrong board/slot, connector/retention damage, excessive force, unexpected power state, boot/link failure, degraded PCIe/link parameters or new errors
Perform one approved cycle only and diagnose before any repeat
Restore retention, cables, cooling clearance and chassis closure before power/reboot
agent_execution_scope: Verify row-2008 variant identity and reject copied PSU-handle scope
Collect and compare pre/post PCIe/Mellanox device identity, firmware, port speed/width/FEC, link/driver counters and unfiltered BMC/host errors
Organize board/slot photos, physical-action/reboot timeline and hashes
Flag changed identity, degraded PCIe or network negotiation, missing detection or incomplete physical proof
Perform no board manipulation, seating verdict, reboot authorization or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact board/slot, traffic/workload drain, safe service sequence, cycle count and recovery plan
Ensure trained operator completes physical inspection/reseat and signs the evidence
Review physical, PCIe and network recovery evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed board/slot checklist with pre/post connector, retention, cable and clearance photos, safe drain/isolation confirmation, one-cycle timeline and correlated PCIe, firmware, port/link/driver/counter/error evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects copied PSU-handle scope and adds BF3-specific PCIe, network and recovery controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Remote enumeration cannot prove edge-connector seating, retention or cable restoration; physical inspection and complete PCIe/network recovery evidence are both required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The board may enumerate at reduced PCIe width or recover only some ports/links. Removal can interrupt multiple paths, damage connectors or disturb cooling.

project_override_considerations: If the platform supports live board replacement, the exact workload drain, redundancy and hot-service sequence must be supplied; otherwise power-isolate. PSU-handle evidence is prohibited.

Operator identity, traffic/workload drain, ESD/power-safe confirmation and labeled before/after photos
Pre/post PCIe width/speed, Mellanox device/firmware/ports/link/FEC/driver/counters, reboot timeline and errors
One-cycle/no-repeat/no-log-clear audit, restored hardware/network state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The exact XLSX item is Mellanox - BF3 Board, but DeepSeek describes Mechanical_Handle - PSU. The primary row and GPT V2 provide coherent board scope, so the copied AI content is isolated.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The authoritative source row is intact and the copied AI scope is repairable by isolation. The case remains MANUAL ONLY with physical execution prerequisites.

review_improvement: Removes the copied PSU-handle procedure, binds the shared code to the BF3 board and adds slot/connector plus PCIe/network recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BF3 board cycle affects both its PCIe function and fabric ports. Simple detection can hide reduced PCIe width, missing functions or degraded link negotiation, while remote state cannot establish physical seating and retention. Therefore physical board/slot evidence must be correlated with exact PCIe and Mellanox identities and full port recovery. A PSU-handle procedure is not transferable because it has different electrical, mechanical and recovery boundaries.
